newsitem.title: UK: Storehouse profits up, H2 encouraging.
newsitem.headline: Storehouse profits up, H2 encouraging.

text.p: British retailer Storehouse Plc on Thursday posted a 13 percent increase in underlying first half profits and said it had had an encouraging start to the second half.

Pretax profits before exceptional items rose to 37.5 million pounds from 33.3 million. Sales increased 14 percent to 590.5 million pounds from 518.8 million. The group took an exceptional charge of 20.5 million pounds following the purchase of Childrens World from Boots Co Plc and the sale of Blazer.
Storehouse, owner of childrenswear chain Mothercare and BhS clothing and homewear stores, raised its interim dividend by 10 percent to 3.3 pence a share.
It said it planned a bigger increase in the final dividend "in the absence of unforeseen circumstances."

Chief executive Keith Edelman said: "Storehouse continues to make good progress. Although the main Christmas trading period has yet to begin the first five weeks of the second half have been encouraging."
Sales at BhS and Mothercare rose by seven percent during the half year, assisted by new stores and overseas franchises.
